claims.summary: Over a commutative coefficient ring, let C be a degree-D pseudoideal and w_1..w_r polynomials. If s has degree <=sigma, s w_i - w_i lies in C for every i and s p lies in C, then f=1-s kills every w_i and f p - p lies in C, so f preserves p modulo C; a sufficient case is s = sum_i a_i w_i with w_i p in C and deg a_i + deg w_i + deg p <= D, and then s^2 = s modulo C when deg a_i + sigma + deg w_i <= D. Over a field, if C is the degree-D part of the vanishing ideal of a finite X and k <= min(D - max deg w_i, D - deg p), a polynomial f of degree <=k kills every w_i with fp outside C exactly when f vanishes on the union Z of the w_i's supports on X and not at every point of supp(p) minus Z; the first such degree is an interpolation degree on X. On the cube 1-s is the reduced product of denominators; for pigeonhole hole factors it is the empty-column indicator.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer; the general form, the (a)-(b) gap and the comparison with the reduced product are its corrections.
claims.rationale: Gives a survival clause for idempotent common killers and the exact first surviving degree in domain models; for Pang's defects reduces a cheap common killer to a cheap OR of the inputs.
claims.next_action: Look for relations among Pang's inputs that make their OR cheap modulo the closure.
